data.note: fault-injection suite for coordination faults on lane fakes

data.found_evidence: Found by the fault suite (XA-coordination-fault-suite, row exit-zero-no-result). A worker script that prints a started and a tool event and then calls sys.exit(0) is read through ProcessHeadless (ddflow/services/lane_headless.py status): LaneStatus(state='exited', exit_code=0, exit_meaning='', detail='', events=2). The same status is returned for a worker that emitted its settled event. Nothing in the status, in budgetstop, in conformance or in the lane sheet says the lane ended without a result; the lease then simply lapses to 'stopped (reason unknown)'. Failing test (red today): run the no_result worker, collect events (no settled among them), then assert not (st.state == 'exited' and st.exit_code == 0 and not st.detail); it fails with "status 'exited' exit 0 detail '': identical to a success". The closed vocabulary of XA-lane-end-record has no class for it (ok | launch_failed | auth | quota_limit | model_unavailable | crash | idle_timeout | lease_lost | budget_stopped | permission_stall | operator_stopped): a no_result class, or status.detail naming the missing settled event, is needed. Next call today: none recorded.

data.title: Lane status cannot tell a settled success from an exit 0 that produced no result

data.body:
Fixes bug Bda514554ae: A lane worker that exits 0 without ever emitting a settled event is reported state exited, identical to a success Found on XA-coordination-fault-suite.

Write the regression test first and watch it FAIL on the unfixed code; then `ddflow complete fix-Bda514554ae --regression-test <test>` closes the bug with the task (or `ddflow bug fixed Bda514554ae --regression-test <test>` first).

Not attached, they match nothing in the tree: tests/test_coordination_faults.py, tests/fixtures/lane_driver/faults.jsonl.
data.title: Fix bug Bda514554ae: Lane status cannot tell a settled success from an exit 0 that produced no result

data.reason: handle-dropped row of the fault table
budget-stop-no-caller row of the fault table

needs a no_result class or a status detail

data.claim: Faults that end the worker process (kill, crash, limit, auth, model, garbage, partial line, silence, ignored cancel) end in a recorded LaneStatus and a lane-sheet resume move; four faults have no record: handle dropped by the launch tick, budgetstop with no caller, no lane.ended event, exit 0 with no result.
data.falsifier: Any listed process fault that hangs past its bound, leaks a process, home or slot, or lacks a status, or any of the four gaps passing its red test.
data.mechanism: ProcessHeadless.status and stop are bounded by idle_s and stop_grace_s and clean the group and home; the ledger turns a lapsed lease into stopped (reason unknown) with an advise resume move; nothing consumes the status after a tick launch (pull._launch_due returns without keeping the Launched), and no event kind for a lane end is registered.
data.probe: uv run pytest tests/test_coordination_faults.py (32 passed in 5.65s); uv run pytest xa/test_fault_defects.py (4 failed: handle dropped, budgetstop no caller, no lane.ended, exit 0 reads as success)

data.question: Do the coordination faults of a spawned worker end in a recorded outcome today, and which have no record?

evidence.note: Research note Rcd4d12949d CONFIRMED: suite 32 passed; scratch red tests 4 failed by name (handle dropped, budgetstop no caller, no lane.ended, exit 0 no result).

Read lane rules and the brief rules (r-bounded-everything, r-unavailable-not-pass, r-docs-with-the-change); edits stay inside the item globs; no knob added; defects filed as bug Bda514554ae and linked to AD-launch-handle-guard, LB-lane-budget-stop, XA-lane-end-record. The memory companion was not consulted.

Committed 39833f046: tests/test_coordination_faults.py (32 tests), tests/fixtures/lane_driver/faults.jsonl, FakeLane hang and ignore_stop, docs/ddflow/lane-conformance.md section. uv run pytest tests/test_coordination_faults.py tests/test_adapter_lanes.py tests/test_ports_contract.py: 262 passed. ruff check clean.

chunk_findings.detail: `test_two_workers_claiming_one_item_is_refused_naming_the_holder` accepts fixture parameters `log` and `cfg` which are undefined in `tests/test_coordination_faults.py` or its imported `lanes_fixture`, causing a NameError or pytest fixture resolution failure when run independently.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_coordination_faults.py:270

chunk_findings.detail: The new hang sleep mishandles a zero idle timeout: `min(idle_s, 1.0) if idle_s else 0.05` treats `idle_s=0` as “not provided” and sleeps 50 ms instead of returning immediately. For example, `lane = FakeLane([], hang=True); h = lane.start(...); list(lane.events(h, idle_s=0.0))` will block for ~0.05 s even though the caller asked for a zero wait, so tests that use `idle_s=0` to poll for “no ended record”/status without waiting become slow or fail elapsed-time assertions.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/fakes/lanes.py:FakeLane.events

chunk_findings.detail: The new text says “Known gaps are named in the table's `defect` column”, but the table immediately above it has only three columns: `fault`, `recorded outcome today`, and `next call`. There is no `defect` column, and the listed known gaps (`Bda514554ae`, `AD-launch-handle-guard`, `LB-lane-budget-stop`, `XA-lane-end-record`) appear only in prose. A reader or tool that follows the documentation and inspects the table to identify expected-failure rows gets no such marker; for example, the dropped-handle gap cannot be located as a table defect as documented.
chunk_findings.title: docs/ddflow/lane-conformance.md (Coordination fault suite known-gaps paragraph)

chunk_findings.detail: The `lease-snapshot-torn` case asserts `end_class":"unchecked"` and an outcome where a torn lease snapshot “allows the call” with a sentence saying it was not checked. For a permission hook, inability to read/check the lease is not permission; if a worker requests a path while the lease snapshot is half-written, this fixture tells the test to accept the call as unchecked rather than refuse/stall it. That encodes a fail-open coordination fault and can let a worker write outside its lease, while also lacking a `defect` marker like the other known-bug lines.
chunk_findings.title: tests/fixtures/lane_driver/faults.jsonl:17

chunk_findings.detail: The `partial-write` case expects `end_class":"ok"` for a process that exits 0 but whose recorded successful events are only `["started"]`, with one skipped partial line. The fixture’s own `exit-zero-no-result` line (line 10) treats a zero exit with no settled result as `end_class":"no_result"`. Given the input “emit `started`, emit a truncated line, exit 0,” this fixture will accept the lane as `ok` even though no `settled` event is present, hiding a lost/never-settled result.
chunk_findings.title: tests/fixtures/lane_driver/faults.jsonl:9

chunk_findings.detail: The `duplicate-launch` case expects `state":"stopped"` together with `end_class":"launch_failed"`, while its outcome says the endpoint slot refuses the second launch. A refused second launch never starts a worker, so the final lane state should be a refusal/no-lane state (as in `missing-auth-key`), not `stopped`. If a test asserts this fixture, it will accept a “stopped” lane record for a launch that never happened, potentially masking a leaked lane/home or misattributed cleanup.
chunk_findings.title: tests/fixtures/lane_driver/faults.jsonl:13

chunk_findings.detail: The change’s stated falsifier is that the “handle dropped” / “no ended record” cases must fail on today’s code, but the executable parametrization removes exactly the rows that document missing records: `PROCESS_ROWS` requires `"defect" not in r`, and the docstring says rows whose end class has no record today carry a `defect`. The only check for those faults is `test_the_table_carries_every_named_fault_once_with_an_outcome`, which merely verifies that the row exists and the defect id is alphanumeric; it never launches a worker, never inspects a lane end record, and never checks that `handle-dropped` is absent from the ledger. Thus, if `faults.jsonl` contains a `handle-dropped` row with a defect id (as required for today’s gap), the suite passes even though the missing-ended-record bug remains unfixed, contradicting the acceptance criterion that this suite is the falsifier.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_coordination_faults.py:PROCESS_ROWS

chunk_findings.detail: Despite the intent requiring each fault to assert the recorded `lane.ended` class, this process-fault test never compares the row’s `end_class` to the handle/status end record. It checks `state`, `exit_code`, `exit_meaning`, `limit`, `reset`, `events`, `skipped`, `dropped`, stop success, and leak removal, but not `end_class`. For a crash row, a driver could return `state="failed"`, `exit_code=2`, `exit_meaning="error"`, and all expected events while recording `lane.ended` as `unknown` or omitting the end record entirely; the test would still pass. The only use of `end_class` is the table existence check, so end-class regressions are not caught.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_coordination_faults.py:test_a_faulty_worker_ends_in_a_recorded_status_and_leaks_nothing

chunk_findings.detail: The test name and acceptance language imply that a second launch under an exhausted endpoint slot is refused, but the test does not pass the capacity pool to the dispatcher: it starts two workers via `driver.start(spec(...))` without `pools`, then manually exercises `CAP.acquire` on a separate pool. A `ProcessHeadless` implementation that ignores capacity and spawns duplicate workers would still pass this test, and the test even asserts that the second worker is running (`driver.status(two).state == "running"`). It therefore verifies only the standalone slot lock primitive, not that the dispatcher refuses duplicate launches or avoids leaking a slot/home/process under real double-launch conditions.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_coordination_faults.py:test_a_second_launch_under_one_name_is_a_distinct_lane_and_the_slot_refuses_it

chunk_findings.detail: The new hang idle wait uses `if idle_s else 0.05`, so a caller-supplied `idle_s=0.0` is treated as “absent” and the fake sleeps 50 ms instead of waiting zero. Given `FakeLane(transcript=[], hang=True)` and a started handle, `list(lane.events(handle, idle_s=0.0))` takes roughly 0.05 s even though the doc says the lane waits out `idle_s`; tests that pass `idle_s=0.0` to avoid wall-clock waits will be slowed and timing assertions can fail.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/fakes/lanes.py:events

chunk_findings.detail: The added prose says “Known gaps are named in the table's `defect` column,” but the table directly above it has only the columns `fault`, `recorded outcome today`, and `next call`; there is no `defect` column. Therefore the named gaps (`Bda514554ae`, `AD-launch-handle-guard`, `LB-lane-budget-stop`, `XA-lane-end-record`) are not actually recorded in the table as the documentation claims, so a reader or tool using the table to locate defect annotations will find none.
chunk_findings.title: docs/ddflow/lane-conformance.md (Coordination fault suite, “Known gaps” paragraph)

chunk_findings.detail: The `partial-write` fixture asserts `end_class: "ok"` even though the scripted worker emits only `["started"]`, one skipped partial line, and exits 0. There is no `settled`/result event, so this is the same class of “exit zero without settling” fault as `exit-zero-no-result` on line 10, which correctly expects `end_class: "no_result"`. With this fixture, a FakeLane that writes a truncated stream line and then exits 0 would be accepted as passed, violating the acceptance requirement that unavailable/never-settled lanes are never reported as passed.
chunk_findings.title: tests/fixtures/lane_driver/faults.jsonl:9

chunk_findings.detail: The `duplicate-launch` fixture says the endpoint slot “refuses” the second launch, but it expects `state: "stopped"`. A refused launch should be modeled like `missing-auth-key` on line 5 (`state: "refused"`, `end_class: "launch_failed"`), not as a lane that started and was later stopped. This fixture would let a test pass when the second launch actually creates a distinct handle/home and is stopped, instead of proving that the duplicate launch is refused before consuming a slot/home/process.
chunk_findings.title: tests/fixtures/lane_driver/faults.jsonl:13

chunk_findings.detail: The suite claims the “handle dropped” / “no ended record” falsifier will fail on today’s code, but no test actually exercises that runtime behavior. `test_the_table_carries_every_named_fault_once_with_an_outcome` only checks that `faults.jsonl` contains a non-empty `end_class` and, if present, a well-formed `defect` id; it never compares that `end_class` to a recorded lane/handle end record. `PROCESS_ROWS` deliberately excludes rows with `defect`, and the process test never reads `lane.ended`, `h.ended`, or `FakeLane._ended`. Thus a fixture row such as `{"fault":"handle-dropped","end_class":"handle_dropped","defect":"XA-lane-end-record",...}` makes the suite pass even though today’s code records no end class for a dropped handle, so the stated falsifier is not implemented and regressions in end-class recording are hidden.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_coordination_faults.py:test_the_table_carries_every_named_fault_once_with_an_outcome

chunk_findings.detail: This test does not actually test duplicate launch under the one-slot capacity pool. It starts both workers with `driver.start(spec(...))` without passing the `CAP.Pool("ep-fault", 1)` endpoint or any capacity context to the lane driver, then manually calls `CAP.acquire(pools, 0, tmp_path / "slots")` twice. If `ProcessHeadless.start` ignores capacity entirely and always spawns, both `driver.start` calls succeed, the manual second `CAP.acquire` still raises `TimeoutError`, the test stops both processes manually, and the test passes. The real duplicate-launch fault is that the second lane should be refused before spawning or cleaned up after a refused slot; the test instead asserts that the second lane is running and that its home still exists, so it can pass while leaking a duplicate process/home.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_coordination_faults.py:test_a_second_launch_under_one_name_is_a_distinct_lane_and_the_slot_refuses_it

chunk_findings.detail: The two `driver.start` calls are outside the `try` block. If the second start raises (for example, because duplicate launch is refused by raising `CapacityError`, or because of an `OSError`), the `finally` that stops `one` is never reached, leaving the first worker process running after the test fails. This contradicts the file’s “no leaked process” requirement; the first handle should be registered for cleanup before the second start is attempted.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_coordination_faults.py:test_a_second_launch_under_one_name_is_a_distinct_lane_and_the_slot_refuses_it
